subsystems.name: Radiation-hardened electronics and sensors
subsystems.role: keep working inside intense gamma and neutron fields.

subsystems.name: Mobility platform
subsystems.role: move over uneven floors, steps and debris without getting stuck.

subsystems.name: Manipulators and tooling
subsystems.role: grasp, cut, drill and sort radioactive components.

subsystems.name: Teleoperation and control
subsystems.role: let a human operator work from a safe distance with enough feedback to be precise.

subsystems.name: Shielding and contamination control
subsystems.role: protect the robot's own electronics and stop radioactive dust spreading.

buildSteps.title: Survey and dose-map the cell
buildSteps.detail: Use existing cameras, LiDAR and dosimeters to build a 3D model and radiation map of the space the robot will enter.

buildSteps.title: Choose radiation-tolerant components
buildSteps.detail: Select motors, cameras and chips rated for the expected total dose, or plan to shield them; standard electronics fail within hours in high fields.

buildSteps.title: Build the chassis
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate a tracked or legged base from steel and aluminium, with sealed bearings and cable routing that can be decontaminated.

buildSteps.title: Integrate arms and tools
buildSteps.detail: Fit manipulators with quick-change couplings so the robot can switch between grippers, cutting tools and vacuum heads.

buildSteps.title: Install electronics and shielding
buildSteps.detail: Place control electronics inside lead or tungsten boxes, run cables through shielded conduits, and add cameras behind lead glass.

buildSteps.title: Write the control software
buildSteps.detail: Implement teleoperation with force feedback, plus collision avoidance and simple autonomy for repetitive cuts.

buildSteps.title: Test in a mock-up
buildSteps.detail: Rehearse every task in a full-size non-radioactive replica of the cell, then dose-test critical parts in a gamma facility.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and operate
buildSteps.detail: Lower or drive the robot into the cell, work remotely in shifts, and monitor its dose and health.

buildSteps.title: Recover and decontaminate
buildSteps.detail: Retrieve the robot, wash or bag it, and either reuse it after decontamination or dispose of it as radioactive waste.

prerequisites.why: semiconductor devices degrade and fail under gamma and neutron dose; hardening adds cost and reduces performance.
haptic feedback and precise control need round-trip delays under about 50 milliseconds; fibre or shielded cable works.
camera sensors darken and lenses brown; shielded cameras and lighting are bulky and still degrade.
hydraulic shears, saws and lasers have been used in nuclear plants for decades.
operators need to plan and train without entering the cell; physics engines model debris and collisions.

pathway.milestone: teleoperated robots perform specific tasks inside damaged or highly radioactive cells, often custom-built for one job
pathway.unlocks: lower radiation dose to human workers and access to spaces people cannot enter.

pathway.milestone: semi-autonomous robots that perform repetitive cutting and sorting with one operator supervising several machines
pathway.unlocks: faster dismantling and lower cost per tonne.

pathway.milestone: modular robot systems that can be airlifted or lowered through narrow openings and decontaminate themselves
pathway.unlocks: reuse of robots across sites instead of one-off builds.

pathway.milestone: fully autonomous decommissioning for standard reactor types
pathway.unlocks: routine, safer and cheaper removal of old reactors.
